message.content:
The question “What is the best movie in 2020?” is inherently subjective—different people value different aspects of a film (story, direction, acting, technical achievement, cultural impact, etc.). Instead of giving a single opinion, here’s an objective overview of the most critically acclaimed and award‑winning films released in 2020, along with the criteria that often influence what people consider “the best.” | Film | Release Year | Key Accolades & Ratings | Why it’s frequently cited as a top 2020 film | |------|--------------|------------------------|---------------------------------------------| | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | 2020 | • 8.2 / 10 on IMDb
• 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• 88 / 100 on Metacritic
• Nominated for 3 Oscars (Best Picture, Best Original Screenplay, Best Supporting Actor) | Widely praised for its sharp script, strong ensemble cast, and timely political relevance. Its high aggregate scores and Oscar nominations place it at the top of many “best of 2020” lists. | | **The Invisible Man** | 2020 | • 7.5 / 10 on IMDb
• 86 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• 73 / 100 on Metacritic | A modern horror‑thriller that revitalized the genre with strong performances (Lily James) and a fresh take on the classic story. It received several award nominations, including a BAFTA for Best Actress. | | **The Gentlemen** | 2020 | • 7.8 / 10 on IMDb
• 84 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• 71 / 100 on Metacritic | Guy Ritchie’s stylish crime comedy was noted for its witty dialogue, ensemble cast, and slick direction. It earned a BAFTA nomination for Best Supporting Actor (Michael Caine). | | **The Irishman** | 2019 (wide release 2020) | • 8.4 / 10 on IMDb
• 96 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• 95 / 100 on Metacritic | Though released in 2019, its Netflix premiere in 2020 gave it a large audience. It won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama and received 10 Oscar nominations. | | **Parasite** | 2019 (wide release 2020) | • 8.6 / 10 on IMDb
• 98 % on Rotten Tomatoes (Critics)
• 96 / 100 on Metacritic | The Korean film that won the Palme d’Or (2019) and the Academy Award for Best Picture (2020). Its critical acclaim and global impact make it a perennial “best” candidate. | ### How “best” is usually measured 1. **Critical consensus** – Aggregated scores from Rotten Tomatoes, Metacritic, and IMDb. 2. **Awards** – Oscars, BAFTAs, Golden Globes, Cannes, etc. 3. **Audience reception** – Box‑office performance, streaming viewership, and social‑media buzz. 4. **Cultural impact** – Influence on public discourse, memes, or industry trends. When you look at the intersection of these metrics, *The Trial of the Chicago 7* emerges as the most frequently cited “best” film of 2020 in mainstream media, film‑review sites, and award ceremonies. However, if you prioritize genre or specific achievements (e.g., horror, comedy, or streaming platform releases), other titles like *The Invisible Man* or *The Gentlemen* might rank higher for you. --- **Bottom line:** - **Most critically acclaimed & award‑winning:** *The Trial of the Chicago 7* - **Best in horror:** *The Invisible Man* - **Best in comedy‑crime:** *The Gentlemen* - **Best overall (including 2019 releases that dominated 2020):** *Parasite* / *The Irishman* Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed comparisons, box‑office data, or a deeper dive into any particular film!
